summary: A player opening the island finds a pretty, warm night: the stone lantern now really glows on the path. They also find nothing new to do. The last seven posts are the same drum motor on the same sand-coloured cylinder. The player still cannot touch it, and since the human's cull Jump in has lost most of its verbs (7 of its 24 tests fail on plugins that no longer exist). The physics underneath is honest and getting deeper (pots that sag, a wound field that is weaker than stones for a real reason), but on screen it is a dark lump on a stump, filmed from the grass.

lighting.why: Night in the raster is the best it has been: the lantern by Lumi throws a real warm pool on the path and the cottage windows glow (reviews/p181/cam-follow-a.png). Noon is still one flat sun: the traced 11:05 still (reviews/p181/drum-traced.png) has no shaped light at all, and the clay lamp lights only its own saucer.

materials.why: Copper windings catch light well in copper-on-iron.png, but the 'cast iron' arch is a matte black box, the block under it a sand-tinted cylinder, the tops board a flat brown 12-gon, the float-top plinth flat slate discs. Nothing on this side of the island shows a path tracer's strengths: no coat, no sheen, no glass, no transmission through the yacht's canvas.

world.why: Same island as s178. The workshop corner by the beach is now crammed: motor bench, pots, drum stump, tops board, magnet plinth, yacht sail and cart road all within 5 m, with no paths, ground cover or reason in their layout (reviews/p181/drum-raster.png).

props.why: The gear wheel and cart are real carpentry. Around them, the drum block, the arch, the tops board and the plinth are bare primitives. 56 generated assets exist; the machine corner uses none.

creatures.why: Faces still read and are charming up close. Two new clips in this review: Pickles stands inside the motor bench table among the pots (drum-traced.png), and the sheep at the workbench has a shovel handle through its face (motion/creatures.png). Several creature close-ups are framed from behind or cut off.

animation.why: The host measure says 10 of 10 move well, but at 02:40 eight of ten were asleep, so it measured almost nothing. Lumi's idle sway in the strip is smooth. The films show the camera popping at their first frame (0.09 change at 0.04 s in two of three films). No new motion work reaches the player.

fun.why: Firefly catch, hide and seek and berry race are unchanged. Jump in lost flight, sneeze, giant and kite with the cull, and T no longer starts a storm (live_tests 'jump': 7 of 24 fail). The machine the last ten sessions built still cannot be touched by the player.

wow.why: Seven posts in a row about the drum motor: lamp, sparks, brushes, gear, cord, copper on iron. 'Copper on iron' is a coil that makes a ninth of the pull, explained in text. A stranger would not share any of them. The nerdy truth in them (the copper eats 18 W the pots can't give) is a great joke that never gets shown on screen.

camera.why: winch-first-haul.mp4: 10 s of lawn with a log, the motor a speck at the horizon. drum-sparks: a top-down view onto the stump. The follow camera's second shot frames a sleeping blob behind bushes (cam-follow-b.png). Every film pops at frame 1.

ui.why: Readable, unchanged. 'Things to try' still promises Jump in keys (6, 7, 8) to a player who cannot find the boards east of the kiln; the panel tells the human about pot voltages, which no player can act on.

style.why: The soft cartoon creatures and painted trees meet bare grey-black engineering primitives in the same frame. No single look.

performance.why: Frame median 4.9 ms, p95 10.6 ms at 30 fps; irondrum is the heaviest system at 1.9 ms p95.

findings.title: Hand the machine to the player: crank, switch, load the cart in Jump in
findings.what: Ten sessions built pots, a drum motor, a winch, a gear and a cart, and the player can do nothing with any of it. Seven posts in a row show it from outside. Meanwhile the s177 cull took flight, sneeze, giant and kite out of Jump in, so the player now has fewer verbs than before.
findings.evidence: NG.live_tests("jump"): 7 of 24 fail (KITE, SNEEZE, GIANT, FLIGHT, STRANGER undefined; 'T did not start a storm'); site posts s174-s181 all drum motor
findings.suggestion: Make it a toy with a programmer's joke in it: Lumi walks to the pots and pulls a plug out of the brine (the cart stops, the volts on a little dial drop), throws the knife switch, puts a stone in the cart and watches it stall on the rise, or swaps stones for the wound field and sees it crawl at 1/9 the pull. Each action changes the real circuit, and the failure is the punchline.
findings.done_when: A FakeInteraction test in Jump in: walk to the switch, press E, the cart moves (position changes > 0.5 m within 10 s); add a load, it stalls. A screenshot shows Lumi's beak on the switch.

findings.title: Winch block, stones and drum still a sand-textured cylinder and black boxes
findings.what: Seventh review in a row: the drum motor stands on a fat brown-sand cylinder, the new 'cast iron' arch is a flat black box, the stones are black cubes. In every post this lump is the hero.
findings.suggestion: Build the block as what a millwright would: a squared oak bed with bolted cheeks, the arch as a cast-iron frame with a fillet, a parting line and a rough sand-cast surface (Hikari conductor with roughness map plus a rust-brown mix at the edges), lodestones as rough faceted magnetite with metallic glints.
findings.done_when: A traced close still at 64+ spp in which a stranger would name the block 'oak' and the arch 'cast iron' without being told; no surface in frame is a primitive with a single flat colour.

findings.title: Creatures overlap: Pickles inside the motor bench, a shovel through the sheep
findings.what: In the traced still Pickles the pig stands inside the motor bench: its legs among the clay pots, the table's legs through its body. On the creature sheet the sheep at the workbench has a shovel handle through its face.
findings.where: separation.jl / avoidance of props in the workshop corner
findings.suggestion: Make the workshop corner's tables, pots, drum and cart road obstacles every creature walks around, and park tools so they don't sit inside a creature at the bench. Better still, let a creature that bumps a pot knock it, so the circuit notices.
findings.done_when: Over 10 min of sandbox time, sampled every second, no creature's bounding sphere overlaps the motor bench, pots, drum block or a held tool by more than 5 cm; a traced still of the corner with creatures around it shows none inside anything.

findings.title: Tops board and float-top plinth are bare flat cylinders on the grass
findings.what: Right beside the machine, the top arena is a 1.4 m flat brown 12-sided disc lying on the lawn, and the float-top plinth is two flat slate discs. From the dashboard camera they are the largest surfaces in frame.
findings.evidence: reviews/p181/drum-raster.png and drum-traced.png (centre and bottom right)
findings.suggestion: Give the tops a real place: a shallow turned bowl of end-grain wood with a lacquer coat (Hikari CoatedDiffuse), worn where tops spin, its rim catching the sun; the magnet plinth as a polished dark stone with a clear coat and a soft reflection of the floating top.
findings.done_when: A traced still of the board shows a dished bowl with a visible specular coat and grain; the outline is round, not a polygon, at 1080p.

findings.title: Machine films: shot from the grass with the motor a speck
findings.what: winch-first-haul.mp4 is 10 s of a flat green lawn and a log crawling towards a motor that is a speck at the horizon. The cart film is better (the camera rides along), but every film starts with a camera pop (0.09 change at 0.04 s).
findings.evidence: reviews/motion/perfectionist-0181/winch-first-haul-overview.jpg; jumps at 0.04 s in all three films
findings.suggestion: Shoot it like a machine film: a low close start on the drum as the rope winds, a pull focus down the taut rope to the log, a cut to the log's end at grass height. Drop the first frame of each render.
findings.done_when: In the overview sheet the motor or the log fills at least a quarter of the frame in 10 of 12 frames; motion_sheet shows no jump above 4x typical in the first 0.5 s.

findings.title: The land yacht's sail is a white board: belly, light through canvas, spoked wheels
findings.what: From the workshop corner the sail is a huge flat beige slab with hard edges that fills a third of the frame. It reads as a wall, not a sail.
findings.suggestion: Model a cambered sail with a belly and a curved leech, and use a thin diffuse-transmission canvas so the sun glows through it, with darker seams and the patch showing as a shadow.
findings.done_when: A traced still against the sun shows the sail lit from behind, with the patch and seams visible as darker shapes, and the outline is curved.

findings.title: The lamp and glowing things light nothing: midday is flat
findings.what: At night the raster is now good: the stone lantern throws a warm pool and the windows glow. At noon the whole workshop corner sits under one flat sun with no contrast, and the clay lamp lights only its saucer, even in the dusk still.
findings.evidence: reviews/p181/drum-traced.png (11:05, flat), reviews/p181/cam-follow-a.png (night, good), site/img/copper-on-iron.png (lamp pool barely reaches the coil)
findings.suggestion: Give the clay lamp a real point light strong enough to put warm light on the copper and long shadows behind the arch at dusk. At noon, use sky light, contact shadows and a warmer bounce off the sand so the corner gets form.
findings.done_when: In a traced dusk still the copper coil facing the lamp is measurably brighter (mean luminance +30%) than the side facing away; in a noon still the shaded side of the drum block is under 50% of the lit side.

findings.title: Jump in: tests and the key card still name the culled plugins
findings.what: After the human removed 50 plugins in s177, the tests for kite, flight, sneeze, giant and stranger still run and fail, and T is still in the tests but no storm comes. The suite's failures are noise that hides real breakage.
findings.evidence: NG.live_tests("jump"): 7 of 24 fail, 5 of them UndefVarError on removed plugins
findings.suggestion: Retire the tests of removed plugins with them, and check that every key named on the Jump in card does something.
findings.done_when: live_tests("jump") passes everything that remains; every key on the Jump in card changes the game state within 2 s in a test.

engine.what: The live eval sandbox module does not see NeverendingGame's unexported names (set_camera! has to be fully qualified), and the clock jumps to 11:00 after a UI test run, so a reviewer's night/day state changes under them.
engine.evidence: live_eval: UndefVarError `set_camera!` not defined in `Main.Live`; clock 02:43 -> 11:03 after live_tests("jump")

process: The author's physics is genuinely good and honest: pots that polarise, a field solver that proves copper is worse than lodestones on six clay cells, and the gear and cart built part by part. That serves the human's long direction (a motor that runs because the simulation makes it run, goal 3). But eight sessions went into one machine that the player cannot touch and that still looks like a stump with black boxes on it. Its posts are seven of the same kind, so goal 8 (radical, unpredictable) is going backwards. Goal 1 (interactions) went backwards too: the cull took Jump in's verbs and nothing replaced them. By goal: goal 2 (a film to be proud of) has no new release since 11-24. Goal 4/7 (rendering, materials) shows only the copper. Goal 5 (Lumi's garden) is alive in the journal voice but not on the island: no bench where Lumi visibly winds that coil. Goal 6 (animation) shows no visible progress. The next sessions should spend one on the look of the machine (#743) and one on making it a toy the player plays with (#643), then leave the motor alone for something nobody would predict.
